facts.statement: Fossils of Jushatyria were found in the Koltaevo III Locality near the Ural Mountains in European Russia.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Koltaevo III Locality, district of Kumertau near the Ural Mountains in European Russia from the Bukobay Gorizont.

facts.statement: Jushatyria lived during the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: The locality dates back to the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Jushatyria is an incomplete left maxilla designated as holotype PIN 2867/5.
facts.quote: Jushatyria is known only from its holotype PIN 2867/5, an incomplete left maxilla.

facts.statement: Jushatyria is classified as an indeterminate archosaur because it possesses an antorbital fossa on the side of its maxilla.
facts.quote: Jushatyria was reassigned as an indeterminate archosaur on the basis of the presence of an antorbital fossa on the lateral surface of the maxilla.

facts.statement: Researchers Nesbitt and Gower and Sennikov suggested that all fossils attributed to Jushatyria may not belong to a single taxon.
facts.quote: Nesbitt (2009) and Gower and Sennikov (2000) suggested that all material currently referred to Jushatyria most likely does not represent a single taxon.

facts.statement: The parent group for Jushatyria is listed as Thecodontia.
Jushatyria is classified within the class Reptilia.
